display.purpose: Hero wordmark and closer statements (Demo Day) only.

label.purpose: Eyebrow tags, HUD chips, table headers, nav links -- always mono, uppercase, tracked out.

shadows.name: key-press-rest

shadows.name: key-press-hover

shadows.name: key-press-active

motion.purpose: Default easing for nearly all transitions site-wide.

motion.name: duration-cta-release

motion.name: duration-cta-press

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one primary action per screen. Cyan fill, hard key-press shadow, inverts on hover, compresses and glows on click.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; position: relative; top: 0; background: #2AE8D2; color: #2B1E1A; border: 2px solid #2B1E1A; padding: 16px 28px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 13px; letter-spacing: 0.12em; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; box-shadow: 0 6px 0 0 #2B1E1A, 0 12px 10px rgba(43,30,26,.25); transition: background-color .32s ease-out, color .32s ease-out, top .32s ease-out, box-shadow .32s ease-out; } .ds-btn-chip { width: 8px; height: 8px; background: currentColor; flex: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #2B1E1A, 0 0 8px 1px currentColor; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #2B1E1A; color: #2AE8D2; top: 2px; box-shadow: 0 4px 0 0 #2B1E1A, 0 6px 10px rgba(43,30,26,.22); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #2AE8D2; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:active { top: 6px; background: #0B6649; color: #F3EEE1; box-shadow: 0 0 0 0 #2B1E1A, 0 0 16px 2px rgba(42,232,210,.55); transition: background-color .04s ease-in, color .04s ease-in, top .04s ease-in, box-shadow .04s ease-in; }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Secondary action -- transparent fill, inverts to solid carbon on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; border: 2px solid #2B1E1A; padding: 16px 28px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 13px; letter-spacing: 0.12em; text-transform: uppercase; background: transparent; color: #2B1E1A; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color .15s cubic-bezier(0.2,0.7,0.2,1), color .15s cubic-bezier(0.2,0.7,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: #2B1E1A; color: #EFE8DA; } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #2AE8D2; outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview: The site's own art-direction brief states it plainly: Gundam x Ghost in the Shell x Voltron, filtered through brutalist editorial layout. Every surface reads like a field manual or mission terminal for a mech pilot: hairline blueprint grids, HUD-style mono labels, engineering-plate tables, and a single frog-shaped mecha rendered with real illustrative weight rather than flat vector iconography. The tension the name captures -- "analog" (paper texture, hand-drafted grid lines, warm printed-matter palette) against "autonomy" (the AI-agent subject matter, cyan status accents, terminal typography) -- is the system's organizing idea, not a decoration on top of a generic SaaS template. Depth comes from borders and hard offsets, never blur. Corners are square everywhere, without exception. Color is disciplined: a warm paper-and-copper base carries almost the entire page, and the one saturated color (cyan) is reserved for AI/system-status meaning, never used decoratively.
keyCharacteristics: Sharp corners only -- zero border-radius anywhere in the system, enforced globally
2px borders as the primary structural/depth device, replacing box-shadow-based elevation
A warm, paper-textured neutral base (grain + scanline overlays at 2-5% opacity) instead of a stark white or black canvas
Cyan is a status/AI-activity signal color, not a general accent -- used sparingly and consistently
Numbered HUD labels (01/02/03) and mono-font engineering tags are load-bearing thematic devices, repeated deliberately across every major section
One real illustrated hero subject (the frog mech + its human pilot) carries the emotional register the copy doesn't reach for alone

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Cyan never appears as generic decoration; every instance means "this is active, primary, or AI-related."

rules.name: The No-Gray Rule
rules.body: There is no neutral gray anywhere in the system. Every "muted" surface is a warm paper or mauve tone; every "dim" text color is a desaturated step of an actual palette hue.

rules.name: The Mono-Means-System Rule
rules.body: IBM Plex Mono is reserved for UI chrome and data. It never appears as a stylistic flourish on body prose.

rules.name: The One Shadow Rule
rules.body: Blur-based shadows do not exist in this system outside the hero wordmark's sticker treatment. If something needs to feel elevated, give it a border and, if it's the primary action, the key-press hard-offset treatment.

dos: Do keep border-radius at 0 everywhere, including on any new component.
Do use 2px carbon borders as the default depth device; reach for the key-press hard-offset shadow only on the single primary action per screen.
Do reserve cyan for AI-activity/status/primary-action meaning; use copper or green for decorative or secondary accents instead.
Do use IBM Plex Mono only for UI chrome, labels, and data -- never for body prose.
Do keep the numbered-label and blueprint-grid HUD motifs consistent if extending them to a new section.
Do keep every nav destination reachable at every viewport width -- collapse into a toggleable panel, never display:none into nothing.
donts: Don't introduce a soft, blurred box-shadow anywhere outside the hero wordmark's sticker treatment.
Don't use gray for "muted" text or surfaces -- desaturate from an existing palette hue instead.
Don't use on-dark-dim as body text color on dark surfaces without checking contrast -- it's documented as a border/divider token, not a text token.
Don't add rounded corners, drop shadows, or gradient fills to any component.
